'''Michael Philip Hartshorn''' (10 September 1936 – 15 December 2017) was a British-born New Zealand [[organic chemist]]. He was awarded the [[Hector Memorial Medal]] by the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1973.

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Keresley]] on the outskirts of [[Coventry]], [[Warwickshire]], England, on 10 September 1936,<ref name="Naturalisation">{{cite web |url=https://search.ancestry.com.au/cgi-bin/sse.dll?indiv=try&db=NZNaturalisations&h=55026 |title=New Zealand, naturalisations, 1843–1981 |year=2010 |publisher=Ancestry.com Operations |access-date=17 December 2017 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Hartshorn was the son of Bernard Hartshorn and Christine Evelyn Hartshorn (née Bennett). He studied at [[Imperial College London]], from where he graduated [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] and [[Associate of the Royal College of Science|ARCS]], and at [[University College, Oxford]], where he obtained a [[DPhil]] in 1960.<ref name="FRSNZ">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/g-i/ |title=All fellows: G–I |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref> His doctoral thesis was titled ''Steroid hormone analogues''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph020435628 |title=Catalogue search |website=SOLO: Search Oxford Libraries Online |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref>

Hartshorn married Jacqueline Joll in 1963, and the couple went on to have four sons.<ref name="Death notice"/> He became a naturalised New Zealand citizen in 1965.<ref name="Naturalisation"/>

==Academic and research career==
Hartshorn was appointed as a lecturer in the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Canterbury]] in [[Christchurch]] in 1960, and rose to become a professor in 1972. When he retired in 1996 he was made a [[professor emeritus]].<ref>{{cite book |chapter=Professores emeriti |title=University of Canterbury Calendar |url=http://www.canterbury.ac.nz/media/documents/academic-services/2006-uc-calendar/calendar01_general_info_staff.pdf |access-date=17 December 2017 |publisher=University of Canterbury |location=Christchurch |page=13}}</ref>

Hartshorn's research centred on [[reaction mechanism]]s. He investigated the chemical rearrangement of [[steroid]]s, cyclic sulfites, [[monoterpene]]s and [[acetylenic]] alcohols. His research included the [[Nitration#Ipso nitration|ipso nitration]] of [[aromatic hydrocarbon]]s and [[phenols]], and their reactions with [[fuming nitric acid]] and [[nitrogen dioxide]], as well as the [[Chlorination reaction|chlorination]] of polysubstituted phenols. He also studied the reactions of cation [[Radical (chemistry)|radicals]] arising from the [[Photodissociation|photolysis]] of aromatic hydrocarbons.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Robinson |first=Ward T. |last2=Edmonds |first2=Michael |last3=Saunders |first3=Darren |date=April 2011 |title=Chemistry in Canterbury: 1986–2010 |url=https://nzic.org.nz/CiNZ/articles/CiNZ%20April%202011%20Edmonds.pdf |journal=Chemistry in New Zealand |publisher=New Zealand Institute of Chemistry |pages=95–101|access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref>

Hartshorn was elected a fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry in 1969, and a fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand the following year.<ref name="FRSNZ"/> In 1973, he received the Hector Memorial Medal,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/hector-medal/recipients-3/ |title=Hector Medal recipients |year=2017 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref> at that time the highest honour for scientific excellence awarded by the Royal Society of New Zealand.

==Death==
Hartshorn died in [[Christchurch]] on 15 December 2017.<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news | url=http://deaths.press.co.nz/obituaries/the-press-nz/obituary.aspx?pid=187540542 | title=Michael Hartshorn death notice | date=16 December 2017 | work=The Press | access-date=17 December 2017}}</ref>
